messages:
Diego: infra-bot just flagged a batch of preemptions in europe-west1, ~28 GPU preempts in last 7m. Seeing increased tail latency for model-serving pods (+180-300ms p95) and a few OOM restarts. Can infra team confirm scope?

infra-bot: [ALERT] 2026-03-18T10:00:12Z - PREEMPTION_BURST - region=europe-west1 pool=spot-gpu-1 count=28 average-notice=14s

Maya: noted. Are these concentrated on a single AZ or spread? Any recent scaling changes? :eyes:

Diego: spread across ew1-b + ew1-c. No rollout at time of spike. Mixed-pool config: 60% preemptible, 40% on-demand for that autoscaling group. Autoscaler logs show many scale-in events right before preempts.

Ken: attaching brief log snippet:
```
2026-03-18T09:54:03Z kubelet: Pod eviction requested: reason=PREEMPTION_SIGNAL
2026-03-18T09:54:07Z model-server: kv-cache flush start
2026-03-18T09:54:09Z model-server: checkpoint failed: context cancelled
2026-03-18T09:54:09Z proxy: 502 upstream closed connection
```

Aisha: looks like we lost warm KV caches causing cold-start latency for affected pods. If prefix caching misses spiked, latency would jump.

Olga: current mitigations we can try now: 1) temporarily reduce batch size to lower memory pressure 2) set routing to prefer on-demand pool for high-latency customers 3) spin up extra on-demand nodes as short-term buffer. Thoughts?

sre-oncall: +1 to buffer. I'll trigger a 20% on-demand scale-up for that region and flip a routing weight for critical routes.

Maya: I'll run a drain exclusion for spot nodes to stop new traffic hitting nodes scheduled for termination:
```
kubectl label node <node> no-serve=true
kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
```

Diego: can someone run a quick tf apply to bump on-demand target capacity? We want this to be automated for next 5-10m then revert.

Ken: running one-off: gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize spot-gpu-group --size=80 -> on-demand-group resize to +8 GPUs. Command:
```
gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize on-demand-gpu-group --size=+8 --region=europe-west1
```

Aisha: Also toggled routing policy to prefer on-demand for /v1/generate and /v1/chat for customers with latency SLOs. Patch config:
```
routeWeights:
  generate:
    on-demand: 0.8
    spot: 0.2
```

infra-bot: [INFO] manual on-demand resize started (request id r-9843). Estimated warm-up ~3m.

Diego: monitoring panels: p50 back to normal quickly but p95 still elevated for some keys. Could be cache rebuild. Any way to speed KV warm-up?

Olga: we can pre-warm caches by replaying recent requests for popular prefixes on new pods. I'll kick a warm-up job that queries top-50 prefixes.

Maya: running warmup job now (job/warmup-eu-179900). Command: kubectl create job --from=cronjob/warmup cron-warmup-1; logs look okay.

Ken: also found the autoscaler was too aggressive: scale-in cool-down set to 30s. Increasing to 5m to avoid thrashing with spot churn. Applying patch to autoscaler config.

Diego: good catch. Please push patch and mention rollback plan.

Ken: patch applied: autoscaler.cooldown=300s. Reverted spot preferred eviction policy to maintain minimal buffer of on-demand 40%.

sre-oncall: traffic routing and on-demand buffer in place. Observability: error rate stable, p95 decreasing from +280ms -> +110ms over last 12m.

Aisha: postmortem items: (1) add signal smoothing to spot-preemption alarms (don't page for <10 preempts in 5m unless p95 impacted) (2) pre-warm KV on new on-demand nodes (3) tune autoscaler cool-down per pool type (4) test routing weight flip in DR runbook.

Diego: agree. Also TODO: evaluate reducing spot fraction in that pool for europe-west1 during business hours; run cost delta calc. Maya, can you own cost vs latency tradeoff doc?

Maya: will do. I'll produce a 1-pager with estimated monthly delta if we drop spot from 60% -> 40% for this pool.

Olga: should we add an emergency runbook step to auto-flip critical routes when preemptions exceed threshold? Could be a simple lambda in ops that runs the weight change and spins up on-demand.

Ken: +1. I'll prototype a tiny service that reacts to infra-bot alerts and applies route overrides with a TTL.

Diego: thanks everyone. For now latency is stabilizing, on-demand buffer holding. Leaving this thread open for any regressions. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: [RESOLVED] 2026-03-18T10:21:39Z - PREEMPTION_BURST - region=europe-west1 - mitigations applied - incident closed.

Olga: filing incident ticket and assigning action items. Will attach perf charts.

Maya: 1-pager ETA 2026-03-18T15:00Z.

Ken: I'll drop the autoscaler cooldown back to 5m permanent and add unit test for cooldown behavior.

Diego: closing—follow-ups in #postmortems. :rotating_light:
